bug_a.title: sh external redirect lossy for externals (w2-make blocker, file-based byte assertion)
bug_a.reported_symptom: w2-make-smoke.log: 'cat HELLO.BIN > CTL.TXT' -> 'cat: : No such file or directory', file created but 0 bytes
bug_a.root_cause: eval_simple() external-fork child did `dup2(lerr, 2)` then `if (lerr != 2) close(lerr)`.  For the 'cmd ARG > FILE 2>&1' shape lerr == 1 (stdout), so the child closed its OWN stdout fd right before execve -> the redirected file received 0 bytes.  The same aliasing existed in the builtin dup-swap cleanup ('2>&1' could close the SHELL's stdout after restore) and in the assignment-only / parent close paths.
bug_a.repro: host build (byte-identical sh.c): `cat HELLO.BIN > F2.TXT 2>&1` -> F2.TXT = 0 bytes, rc=0.  Deterministic.
bug_a.fix: guard every redirect-close in eval_simple with '>= 3': fds 0/1/2 are the shell's own stdio and must survive a dup; only the fds apply_redirs() OPENED (always >= 3) are closed after dup2.  Four sites: assignment-only early return, builtin dup-swap cleanup, external-fork child, parent finally.

bug_b.title: shell_test 'FAILED echo validation' / shell_test3 'FAILED cat nested.txt' ambient FAIL tokens under thread-slot pressure (used=63/63)
bug_b.root_cause: read_until('$ ') terminates at the FIRST prompt it sees.  Under the wave-start thread-slot-pressure storm ('[KERNEL] thread_create: no free slot (used=63/63)'), a command's output arrives LATE; the next step's read consumes a STALE prompt from the previous command, the needle check misses, and the plain echo/clear/cat-nested steps had NO retry and NO pressure classifier -> hard FAIL.
bug_b.fix: drain_pending() before every command write (each read owns exactly its command's output); run_builtin_check() for echo/clear (drain + retry + pressure-classified SKIP instead of hard FAIL); deadline-bounded + drained reads for the nested-file echo and every sequence in shell_test2/3.
